subject.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels

question: Should CLI reseed history consume only canonical `__openclaw` sender metadata as untrusted presentation, or may arbitrary top-level sender fields override that persisted identity?
rationale: Current main has an approved durable envelope contract, while this PR adds a second higher-priority source and model-visible identity wording; repository history does not establish that trust and precedence choice automatically.

options.title: Use the canonical envelope
options.body: Read the approved `__openclaw` sender fields through a shared resolver, present them as untrusted participant context, and remove top-level override behavior.

options.title: Approve dual-source precedence
options.body: Keep top-level-first resolution, but explicitly approve its trust boundary and add tests proving override, hook, duplicate-name, and spoof-resistant behavior.

options.title: Pause for broader attribution design
options.body: Hold this renderer change until sender attribution, owner status, and trusted inbound metadata share one cross-consumer contract.

recommendation.title: Use the canonical envelope
recommendation.body: Read the approved `__openclaw` sender fields through a shared resolver, present them as untrusted participant context, and remove top-level override behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged persistence work defines the canonical sender metadata and redaction boundary this decision must extend.
